answer: Latency-shadow admission: each new identity must broadcast its first actions on a fixed delay schedule, and the network scores arrivals by how evenly they spread across slots. A burst that fills one slot looks hollow later when the same cluster's traffic fails to fill the following slots, so admission is denied until the pattern completes. Genuine users generate a natural ripple across slots, while a farm must either slow to one identity per slot—costing operator time and idle capacity—or pay to keep many identities warm through the full trellis of slots before earning any throughput.
